explanation: Allocate one height for every integer position from the leftmost building to the rightmost building. Raise each covered position to the maximum building height, then compress equal adjacent heights into maximal inclusive spans.
timeComplexity: O(n+W+Σwidth): n buildings, W=maxRight−minLeft+1 coordinate positions, and width=right−left+1 for each building. Filling every covered coordinate can cost O(nW).
spaceComplexity: O(W) height storage and at most O(W) emitted runs; this implementation depends on coordinate span, not just building count.

correctness: After processing a prefix of buildings, each height is the maximum of all processed buildings covering that integer position. Thus after all buildings it is the skyline height. The final scan emits a span exactly when the height changes, yielding every maximal run, including internal zero-height gaps.
walkthrough: Buildings [1,1,4] and [3,3,2] produce a coordinate height array [4,0,2] at positions 1,2,3. Both adjacent boundaries change height, so emit [1,1,4], [2,2,0], [3,3,2].
edgeCases: Uncovered internal gaps are emitted at height zero.
Repeated equal heights require multiplicity counts, not just a set.
